mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {طوى}: whoever leaves it without tanwīn, his reason is that it is deflected (maʿdūl), like عمر, and it is definite; and it is said that it is feminine, a name of the spot of land, and it is definite. Whoever gives it tanwīn makes it a name of the place, not deflected, like صُرَد. In both views it is a badal (substitute) from الْوَادي.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {وَمَا تِلْكَ بيمينك}: تِلْكَ according to al-Zajjāj has the meaning of الَّتِي (relative noun), and بيمينك is its ṣila (relative clause). According to al-Farrāʾ it has the meaning of هَذِه, and هَذِه and تلك according to him require a ṣila like الَّتِي. Quṭrub reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that تِلْكَ has the meaning of هَذِه. مَا is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is the khabar (predicate). The meaning of the interrogative here is to draw attention (tanbīh).

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying {تخرج بَيْضَاء}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in تخرج. آية is a badal (substitute) from بَيْضَاء, likewise a ḥāl, i.e. it comes out making clear the power of Allah (exalted be His mention). It is also said that آية is accusative by an implied verb, the implied form being "We have given you another sign" (آتيناك آيَة أُخْرَى). The nominative is permissible outside the Qurʾān, on the sense "this is a sign" (هَذِه آيَة).

mekki-muskil:29-30.t: His saying {وَاجعَل لي وزيرا من أَهلِي هَارُون}: هَارُون is a badal (substitute) from وزير; and it is said to be accusative by اجعل with fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), i.e. "and make Hārūn, my brother, a minister for me" (وَاجعَل لي هَارُون أخي وزيرا).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying, the Exalted, {إِلَّا تذكرة}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or as a maṣdar (verbal noun). And تنزيلا is a maṣdar.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t:
His saying {نسبحك كثيرا}: كثيرا is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "that we may glorify You with much glorification" (نسبحك تسبيحا كثيرا), or a naʿt of an omitted time, its implied form being "that we may glorify You a long time" (نسبحك وقتا طَويلا).
Whoever reads with the connecting alif in اشْدُد and with fatḥa on the alif of أشركه makes it a supplication and request, so it is indeclinable (mabnī). Whoever reads with the disjunctive alif in اشْدُد and ḍamma on the alif of أشركه — and that is Ibn ʿĀmir — makes it jussive (majzūm) as the answer to اجعل [Translator's note: the source writes لأجعل], so the two alifs are the alifs of the first person. In the first reading, the first alif is a connecting alif (alif waṣl) and the second a disjunctive alif (alif qaṭʿ).

mekki-muskil:39-39.t: His saying {أَن اقذفيه فِي التابوت فاقذفيه فِي اليم}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from مَا. The first hāʾ in اقذفيه refers to Mūsā (peace be upon him), and the second to the chest (التابوت).

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {فِي كتاب لَا يضل رَبِّي وَلَا ينسى}: what comes after كتاب, of the two clauses, is a description (ṣifa) of it. رَبِّي is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, its implied form being "the Book does not stray from my Lord, nor forget" (لَا يضل الْكتاب عَن رَبِّي وَلَا ينسى). It may also be that رَبِّي is in the position of the nominative, straying and forgetting being denied of Him. We have explained this verse in the book al-Hidāya more fully than this.

mekki-muskil:58-58.t:
His saying {مَكَانا سوى}: مكان is accusative as the second object of جعل. It may not be made accusative by الْموعد, because it has been described by His saying, the Exalted,
{لَا نخلفه نَحن وَلَا أَنْت}; and nouns that govern as verbs do, when they are described or made diminutive, do not govern, because by description and diminution they leave their resemblance to verbs, since verbs are neither described nor made diminutive. So when, by description and diminution, they leave the resemblance to the verb, they are barred from governing. This is a principle on which the Basrans do not differ. Likewise, when you predicate something of maṣdars (verbal nouns) or conjoin something to them, it is not permissible to make them govern anything after that, because you would be separating the ṣila from the mawṣūl (the relative) — for what is governed is included in the ṣila of the maṣdar, whereas the khabar and the conjoined are not included in the ṣila. Nor is it good for مَكَانا in this place to be an adverb (ẓarf), because the Arabs did not treat الْموعد with adverbs as they treat the other maṣdars with them. Do you not see that He, the Exalted, said {إِن موعدهم الصُّبْح} with the nominative? Had you said إن خروجهم الصبح, nothing but the accusative would be allowed in الصبح, on the implied form "the time of the morning". And الْموعد has come as a noun of place: Allah (exalted be His mention) said {وَإِن جَهَنَّم لموعدهم أَجْمَعِينَ}, and it has been said that its meaning is "the place of their appointment".
And His saying {سوى}: it is a description (ṣifa) of مكان. But whoever reads the sīn with kasra makes it rare, because فِعَل has come as an adjective only rarely, as in هم قوم عِدًى ("they are a hostile people"). Whoever reads the sīn with ḍamma brings it on the more common pattern, because فُعَل is frequent among adjectives, e.g. رجل حُطَم, لُبَد and شُكَع, and it is frequent.

mekki-muskil:102-102.t: His saying {زرقا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْمُجْرمين.

mekki-muskil:59-59.t:
His saying {مَوْعدكُمْ يَوْم الزِّينَة}: the nominative in يَوْم is as the khabar (predicate) of مَوْعدكُمْ, on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "your appointment is the time of the day of adornment" (مَوْعدكُمْ وَقت يَوْم الزِّينَة). Al-Ḥasan read يَوْم الزِّينَة in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf).
And His saying {وَأَن يحْشر النَّاس ضحى}: أَن is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to يَوْم, on the implied form "your appointment is the time of the day of adornment and the time of the gathering of the people". It is also said that أَن is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to الزِّينَة. Whoever reads يَوْم الزِّينَة in the accusative makes أَن in the position of the accusative, conjoined to يَوْم الزِّينَة; and it may be in the position of the nominative on the implied form "your appointment is the time of the gathering of the people", or in the position of the genitive, conjoined to الزِّينَة.

mekki-muskil:63-63.t:
His saying {إِن هَذَانِ لساحران}: whoever reads هَذَانِ in the nominative takes it according to a dialect of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb, who bring the dual with alif in every state. One of them said:
... تزَود منا بَين أذنَاهُ طعنة ... دَعَتْهُ هابي التُّرَاب عقيم ...
(He took from us, between his ears, a thrust as provision that called him to the dusty, barren earth.)
It is said that إِن has the meaning of نعم ("yes"); and there is remoteness (improbability) in this because of the entry of the lām into the khabar (predicate), and that occurs only in poetry, as in his saying:
... أم الْحُلَيْس لعجوز شهربه ... ترْضى من اللَّحْم بِعظم الرقبه ...
(Umm al-Ḥulays is surely an old crone, content, of meat, with the bone of the neck.)
The proper form of the speech would have been لأم الْحُلَيْس عَجُوز. Likewise the proper form of the speech in the verse, if you take إن in the meaning of نعم, would have been إِن لهذان ساحران, as you say نعم لهذان ساحران and نعم لمُحَمد رَسُول الله. And in the lām coming late together with the word إن there is some strength for [the view of] نعم.
It is said that since the vague nouns (al-mubham, i.e. demonstratives) show no inflection in the singular or in the plural, the dual was treated likewise, and the alif was brought in every state. And it is said that the hāʾ [of the pronoun] is implied with إن, its implied form being إِنَّه هَذَانِ لساحران, as you say إِنَّه زيد منطلق; and this is a good view, were it not that the entry of the lām into the khabar makes it remote.
As for whoever reads إن light (without doubling), it is a good reading, because he set the i'rab right and did not contradict the script; but the entry of the lām into the khabar opposes it according to the school of Sībawayh, because he assumes it is the one lightened from the heavy [إنّ], so that what follows it became nominative as mubtadaʾ and khabar because of the deficiency of its form, and what follows it returned to its origin; and the lām does not enter the khabar of a mubtadaʾ that has come in its original form, except in poetry, as we mentioned. But according to the school of the Kufans it is among the best of things, because they take the light إن in the meaning of مَا and the lām in the meaning of إِلَّا, so the implied form of the speech is "these two are nothing but two sorcerers" (مَا هَذَانِ إِلَّا ساحران). There is no defect in this interpretation except what they claim, that the lām comes in the meaning of إِلَّا.

mekki-muskil:66-66.t: His saying {يخيل إِلَيْهِ من سحرهم أَنَّهَا تسْعَى}: whoever reads يخيل with yāʾ makes أَن in the position of the nominative, because it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of يُخيَّل. Whoever reads تخيل with tāʾ — and that is Ibn Dhakwān — makes أَن in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the latent pronoun in تخيل, and it is a substitute of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). The like of that is permissible in the reading of whoever reads with yāʾ, on the basis that you make the verb masculine according to the meaning. It is also possible that أَن, in the reading of whoever reads with tāʾ, is in the position of the accusative on the assumption of the omission of the bāʾ [Translator's note: the source writes خذف for حذف], its implied form being "it was made to seem to him by their magic that it was moving" (تخيل اليه من سحرهم بِأَنَّهَا تسْعَى), and you make the maṣdar or إليه in the position of the nāʾib fāʿil.

mekki-muskil:67-67.t: His saying {فأوجس فِي نَفسه خيفة مُوسَى}: مُوسَى is in the position of the nominative by أوجس, and خيفة is the object of أوجس. The origin of خيفة is خوفة; then the wāw was replaced by a yāʾ and what precedes it given kasra so that the pattern فِعْلة would be sound. Mūsā only feared that the people would be led astray; and it is said that when the revelation to throw his staff was slow to come to him, he feared; and it is said rather that human nature overcame him on seeing what he was not accustomed to. And Allah knows best.

mekki-muskil:69-69.t:
His saying {وألق مَا فِي يَمِينك تلقف مَا صَنَعُوا}: whoever reads تلقف in the jussive makes it the answer to the imperative. Whoever reads it in the nominative — and that is Ibn Dhakwān — makes it nominative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from مَا, which is the staff; and it is said to be a ḥāl from the one throwing, who is Mūsā, the swallowing being attributed to him since it came about through his action and movement, as He said {وَمَا رميت إِذْ رميت وَلَكِن الله رمى}. It is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because it only swallowed their ropes after he had thrown it.
His saying {إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا كيد سَاحر}: مَا is the noun of إِن, with the meaning of الَّذِي, and كيد is its khabar; the hāʾ is omitted from صَنَعُوا, its implied form being "that which they have made is the trick of a sorcerer" (إِن الَّذِي صنعوه كيد سَاحر). Whoever reads كيد سحر, its meaning is "the trick of one possessing sorcery". It is permissible in ordinary speech to make كيد accusative by صنعوا and not to imply a hāʾ, on the basis that you make مَا the restraining (kāffa) particle that stops إن from governing. And it is permissible to read أَن with fatḥa, in the meaning "because what they have made…" (لِأَن مَا صَنَعُوا).

mekki-muskil:72-72.t:
His saying {إِنَّمَا تقضي هَذِه الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا}: مَا is the restraining (kāffa) particle that stops إن from governing, and هَذِه is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and الْحَيَاة is a badal (substitute) from هَذِه or a naʿt (adjective), its implied form being "you will only decree in this worldly life" (انما تقضى فِي هَذِه الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا). It is permissible in ordinary speech to put هَذِه and الْحَيَاة in the nominative, on the basis that you make مَا have the meaning of الَّذِي, with the hāʾ omitted with تقضى, and هَذِه is the khabar of إن [Translator's note: the source has خبز ان, evidently for خبر إن], and الْحَيَاة is a badal from هَذِه or a naʿt, its implied form being "that which you decree is the matter of this worldly life" (ان الَّذِي تقضيه أَمر هَذِه الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا).
His saying {وَالَّذِي فطرنا}: الَّذِي is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to مَا; or, if you wish, as an oath.

mekki-muskil:73-73.t: His saying {وَمَا أكرهتنا عَلَيْهِ}: مَا is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to الْخَطَايَا; and it is said to be a negating particle. If you make مَا negating, مِن is attached to (mutaʿalliq) الخطايا; and if you make مَا have the meaning of الَّذِي, مِن is attached to أكرهتنا.

mekki-muskil:77-77.t:
His saying {لَا تخَاف دركا وَلَا تخشى}: whoever reads تخَاف in the nominative makes it a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent, who is Mūsā (peace be upon him), and the implied form is "strike for them a path in the sea, not fearing being overtaken nor dreading" (اضْرِب لَهُم طَرِيقا فِي الْبَحْر غير خَائِف دركا وَلَا خاشيا). The nominative of تخاف is strengthened by the consensus of the readers on the nominative of تخشى, which is conjoined to تخاف. It is permissible to read تخَاف in the nominative as a break (qaṭʿ, a new sentence), i.e. "you do not fear being overtaken" (أَنْت لَا تخَاف دركا). It is also said that its nominative is as a naʿt (adjective) of طريق, on the assumption of the omission of فيه ("in which"). Whoever reads تخاف in the jussive — and that is Ḥamza — makes it the answer to the imperative, which is فَاضْرب, and the implied form is "if you strike, you will not fear being overtaken by those behind you" (إِن تضرب لَا تخف دركا مِمَّن خَلفك); and وَلَا تخشى is nominative as a break, i.e. "and you do not dread drowning". It is also said that the jussive in لَا تخف is as a prohibition. Al-Farrāʾ permitted وَلَا تخشى to be in the position of the jussive with the alif retained, as the yāʾ and the wāw are retained on the assumption that the vowel has been dropped from them. But this is not permissible with the alif, because it never takes a vowel except by being changed into something else, whereas the wāw and the yāʾ take vowels without being changed.
His saying {ألم يَعدكُم ربكُم وَعدا حسنا}: الْوَعْد may have the meaning of "what is promised" (الْمَوْعُود), just as الْخلق came with the meaning of "what is created" (الْمَخْلُوق); so وَعدا on this interpretation is accusative as the second object of يعدكم, on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "Did your Lord not promise you the fulfilment of a good promise?" (ألم يَعدكُم ربكُم تَمام وعد حسن). And وعد may be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:80-80.t: His saying {وواعدناكم جَانب الطّور الْأَيْمن}: جَانب is accusative as the second object of واعد. It is not good for it to be accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), because it is a specific, not vague, adverb of place; verbs and maṣdars pass to adverbs of place without a preposition only when they are vague. This is a principle on which there is no disagreement. The implied form of the verse is "and We made an appointment with you for coming to the right side of the Mount" (وواعدناكم إتيان جَانب الطّور), then the muḍāf was omitted.

mekki-muskil:87-87.t:
His saying {مَا أخلفنا موعدك بملكنا}: الْملك is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the reading of whoever reads the mīm with ḍamma, fatḥa or kasra, and these are dialectal variants. The implied form is "we did not break our appointment with you by our possession of what is right; rather we broke it through our sin" (مَا أخلفنا موعدك بملكنا الصَّوَاب بل أخلفناه بخطيئتنا). The maṣdar here is annexed to the agent and the object is omitted, just as elsewhere it is annexed to the object and the agent omitted, as in His saying, the Exalted, {بسؤال نعجتك} and His saying {دُعَاء الْخَيْر}. It is also said that whoever reads it with ḍamma on the mīm makes it the maṣdar of their saying هُوَ مَلِك بَيِّن الْمُلك ("he is a king of evident kingship"); whoever reads with kasra makes it the maṣdar of هُوَ مَالك بَيِّن الْمِلك ("he is an owner of evident ownership"); and whoever reads with fatḥa makes it a noun.
His saying {فَكَذَلِك ألْقى السامري}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "so the Sāmirī threw a throwing like that" (فَألْقى السامري إلقاء كَذَلِك).

mekki-muskil:94-94.t: His saying {يَا ابْن أم}: whoever reads the mīm with fatḥa intends يَا بن أُمِّي; then the yāʾ of annexation was replaced by an alif, then the alif was dropped for lightness because the fatḥa indicates it. It is also said rather that he made the two nouns one noun and made them indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa. Whoever reads the mīm with kasra does so on the basis of the original annexation, but dropped the yāʾ because the kasra indicates it. The original would have been to retain it, because الْأُم is not the one addressed (munādā); the one addressed is only الابن, and dropping the yāʾ is only good and preferred with the one addressed itself, and الأم is not addressed.

mekki-muskil:97-97.t: His saying {لن تخلفه}: whoever reads it with kasra on the lām (لن تُخلِفَه), it is in the meaning "you will not find it broken", as you say أحمدته, i.e. "I found him praiseworthy". It is also said that its meaning is taken as a threat, i.e. "you must inevitably come to it". Whoever reads it with fatḥa on the lām (لن تُخلَفَه), its meaning is "Allah will not fail to fulfil it for you", and the one addressed is a latent pronoun as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), the agent being Allah, glorified and exalted be He, and the hāʾ is the second object. The one addressed in the first reading is the agent in both meanings. أخلف takes two objects, and the second is omitted in the reading of whoever reads with kasra on the lām; the implied form is "you will not cause Allah to break the appointment which He decreed that you will come to" (لن تخلف أَنْت الله الْموعد الَّذِي قدر أَن ستأتيه).

mekki-muskil:99-99.t: His saying {كَذَلِك نقص عَلَيْك}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "We narrate to you a narrating like that" (نقص عَلَيْك قصصا كَذَلِك).

mekki-muskil:103-103.t: His saying {إِلَّا عشرا}: accusative by لبثتم.

mekki-muskil:118-118.t:
His saying {إِن لَك أَلا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative because it is the noun of إِن.
Whoever reads with fatḥa {وَأَنَّك لَا تظمأ} conjoins it to أَن لَا, its implied form being "and it is for you to have no hunger and no thirst in Paradise" (وَإِن لَك عدم الْجُوع وَعدم الظمأ فِي الْجنَّة). It is also possible that the second أَن is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the position [of the noun of إنّ]. Whoever reads it with kasra does so as a new beginning (istiʾnāf) [Translator's note: the source has الِاسْتِثْنَاء "exception", evidently for الاستئناف].

mekki-muskil:128-128.t: His saying {أفلم يهد لَهُم كم أهلكنا}: the fāʿil (agent) of يهد is implied, and it is the maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "has the guidance not guided them?" (أفلم يهد الْهدى لَهُم). It is also said that the agent is implied on the assumption of "the matter", its implied form being "has the matter not made it clear to them how many We destroyed?" (أفلم يهد الْأَمر لَهُم كم أهلكنا). The Kufans said: كم is the agent of يهد; and this is a mistake according to the Basrans, because كم has the front of the sentence and what precedes it cannot govern it; only what follows it governs it, like أيّ in the interrogative. The governing word (ʿāmil) of كم, that which makes it accusative, according to the Basrans, is أهلكنا.

mekki-muskil:131-131.t:
His saying {زهرَة الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا}: زهرة is made accusative by an implied verb indicated by متعنَا, because متعنَا is in the position of جعلنَا; so it is as though He said "We made for them the flower of the worldly life" (جعلنَا لَهُم زهرَة الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا). This is the view of al-Zajjāj. It is also said that it is a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ in بِهِ according to its position, as you say مَرَرْت بِهِ أَخَاك ("I passed by him, your brother"). Al-Farrāʾ indicated that its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial), with متعنَا governing it; he said: as you say مَرَرْت بِهِ الْمِسْكِين ("I passed by him, the poor one"); and he took its implied form to be "We let them enjoy it as an adornment in the worldly life and a decoration in it" (متعناهم بِهِ زهرَة فِي الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا وزينة فِيهَا). He said: [this is so] even if it is definite, for the Arabs say مَرَرْت بِهِ الشريف الْكَرِيم, meaning that you make it accusative as a ḥāl on the assumption that the alif and lām are redundant. It is also possible to make زهرة accusative on the basis that it is put in the place of the maṣdar (verbal noun), and in the place of زِينَة, like {صنع الله} and {وعد الله}; and there is room for consideration in this.
Abū Muḥammad [Makkī] said: the best is to make زهرة accusative as a ḥāl, with the tanwīn dropped because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the lām of الْحَيَاة — as it has been read {وَلَا اللَّيْل سَابق النَّهَار} with النَّهَار in the accusative by سابق, on the assumption that the tanwīn was dropped because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the lām. Then الْحَيَاة is in the genitive as a badal from مَا in His saying إِلَى مَا متعنَا, so the implied form is "and do not extend your eyes towards the worldly life as an adornment", i.e. in the state of its adornment. It is not good for زهرة to be a badal from مَا according to its position in His saying إلى مَا متعنَا, because لنفتنهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) متعنا, so it is included in the ṣila (relative clause) of مَا; and لنفتنهم is also included in the ṣila, and the substitute may not come before what is in the ṣila, because the badal can only come after the ṣila of the one substituted for is complete. So the substitution of زهرة from مَا according to its position is barred.

mekki-muskil:133-133.t: His saying {بَيِّنَة مَا}: مَا is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of الْبَيِّنَة to it. Al-Kisāʾī permitted tanwīn on بَيِّنَة, so that مَا would be a badal (substitute) from بَيِّنَة.

mekki-muskil:135-135.t: His saying {فستعلمون من أَصْحَاب}: مَن is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and ستعلمون does not govern it, because it is an interrogative, and what precedes an interrogative does not govern it. Al-Farrāʾ permitted مَن to be in the position of the accusative by يستعملون [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for ستعلمون], taking it as other than an interrogative and making مَن for the genus, as in His saying, the Exalted, {وَالله يعلم الْمُفْسد من المصلح}.
